title: Hand-plant the second strawberry row, staggered against the machine-set row
instruction: The transplanter set the far row of strawberry plugs on this bed; plant the near row by hand. Stand one plug from the grey trays upright on the bed level with the middle of each gap in the far row, so the two rows are staggered, as far on the near side of the blue drip tape as the far row is on the other side. Do not disturb the far row.
context: Strawberry plasticulture. Annual strawberries grow on raised beds under black plastic mulch as a double row either side of the drip tape on the bed's centre line, the rows about 12 in apart and the plants about 12 in apart in the row, staggered: each plant stands level with the middle of a gap in the other row, so every plant gets the most room. A two-row transplanter sets both rows; when one of its planting units jams for a stretch, the crew behind it plants that stretch by hand to match the other row (Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, O*NET 45-2092). Nothing on the bed marks where the hand-set plants go: along the row they are read from the other row's gaps, across the bed by mirroring that row in the drip tape. Here, at 1:3, the far row stands 50 mm beyond the tape, so the near row goes 50 mm on this side, level with its five gaps; each arm naturally plants from the tray on its own side.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A strawberry bed at 1:3 scale (100 mm here is about 12 in); four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Bed: a raised bed fixed to the table, 220 mm across (along x), 600 mm long (along y) and 25 mm tall, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0 (x 19.0 to 41.0 cm, y -30.0 to +30.0 cm); its flat top is black plastic mulch (in a real build, black plastic sheet over a board). (2) Drip tape: a blue strip 16 mm wide along the bed's centre line (x 29.2 to 30.8 cm) for the whole length of the bed, flush with the mulch (in a real build, blue adhesive tape); in simulation the bed is three boxes with one flush top, the black near half, the blue tape and the black far half. (3) Two plug trays: light-grey rigid plastic plates fixed to the table, 160 mm along x, 50 mm along y and 5 mm thick, centred at x 20.0 cm, y +36.0 cm (left) and y -36.0 cm (right). (4) Twelve strawberry plugs, all alike and interchangeable: loose green cylinders 30 mm across and 45 mm tall, 25 g each, each standing on end (a plug plant, its root ball and crown; in a real build green-painted hardwood dowels, the same either end up). Six stand on the bed as the far row the transplanter set: centres at x 35.0 cm (50 mm beyond the tape's centre line), y +25, +15, +5, -5, -15 and -25 cm, 100 mm apart with five gaps between them. Three stand on each tray, centres at x 14.0, 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y +36.0 cm (left tray) and y -36.0 cm (right tray). Nothing else is on the table. The near row the instruction asks for has one plug level with the middle of each gap in the far row, as far on this side of the tape as the far row is on the other: centres at x 25.0 cm, y +20, +10, 0, -10 and -20 cm. None of the five places is marked; six plugs on the trays for five places leave one spare, and any plug may fill any place.
scoring: End state: the score is read from where the twelve plugs stand at the last step; they are identical, so it never asks which plug is which. A plug is 'planted' when its centre, seen from above, is over the bed's top, its lowest point is within 3 mm of that top and its axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either end up). The far row is kept when each of its six spots still has a planted plug with its centre within 10 mm of the spot's centre, measured flat. A place is 'filled' when a planted plug has its centre within 15 mm of the place's centre, measured flat (the places are 100 mm apart, so no plug is within 15 mm of two). Score 0 if the far row is not kept (a far plant knocked over, shoved, lifted or taken away and its spot left empty), or if any plug is off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise the score is 0.2 for each filled place: 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 or 1.0. A plug left on its tray, on the table, lying on the bed, standing on the bed away from every place and spot, standing on another plug or held above the bed fills nothing and costs nothing; a far plant moved to a place with a tray plug stood on its spot leaves the same bed and scores the same. Every outcome: the start 0; a near row set in line with the far plants (y +-5, +-15, +-25 cm, 50 mm off every place) 0; a near row on the drip tape (x 30.0 cm, 50 mm off) 0; a staggered row 100 mm in front of the tape (x 20.0 cm) 0; one, two, three or four places filled 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 or 0.8; all five 1.0; any of these with a far-row spot left empty or a plug off the table 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held with every plug still (its centre moving less than 5 mm in all over the last 0.5 s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, find each place by tape from the bed's fixed edges (60 mm from its near edge; 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 mm from its left end) and lay a ring template 60 mm across on it: the place is filled if a plug stands upright with its base wholly inside (centre within 15 mm). Before the first trial draw a chalk circle 50 mm across round each far plant's spot; after a trial each circle must hold a plug standing upright with its base wholly inside (within 10 mm).
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. The bed and trays are fixed boxes; each plug is a plain uniform cylinder, the same either end up, standing on the mulch (no planting hole, soil, roots or leaves; real plugs go crown up into holes punched in the plastic). Real drip tape runs under the mulch on the bed's centre line; here it is a blue strip so it can be seen (also half-way between the bed's long edges). The scorer sees only the plugs, so one held still in place counts as planted.
reset_notes: Stand six plugs back upright on the bed at x 35.0 cm, y +25, +15, +5, -5, -15 and -25 cm (inside the chalk circles drawn round those spots before the first trial), and three upright on each tray at x 14.0, 20.0 and 26.0 cm, y +36.0 cm (left) and -36.0 cm (right). The plugs are interchangeable; the bed, drip tape and trays are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
